data.reasoning: The package is a standard AUR icon theme package. The PKGBUILD fetches a tarball from the official Linux Mint repository (packages.linuxmint.com) with a pinned SHA-256 checksum, contains only variable assignments and a simple package() function that copies files. The .SRCINFO is standard metadata. No malicious code, no suspicious network operations, no injection patterns. The 'inconclusive' verdicts were caused by tool errors (API failures and parse errors), not security concerns. The deepseek model successfully reviewed both files and correctly identified the package as safe.
data.disagreement_analysis: The disagreement was caused by tool errors, not substantive security findings. The qwen model encountered an HTTP 400 API error when reviewing the PKGBUILD (though its initial audit succeeded and found it safe). The openrouter/free model had a parse error on .SRCINFO (the model returned 'User Safety: safe' instead of proper XML). Only the deepseek model successfully completed the full audit. All models that successfully reviewed the PKGBUILD found it safe.
coverage_issues: qwen model: PKGBUILD review failed with HTTP 400 error during full review phase, despite successful initial audit
openrouter/free model: .SRCINFO review failed due to parse error (model output format mismatch)
learnings: When a model fails during full file review, check if an earlier audit phase (e.g., initial PKGBUILD audit) succeeded and use that result instead of marking inconclusive
Implement retry logic or fallback parsers when models return non-standard output formats (like 'User Safety: safe' instead of XML)
Tool errors (API failures, parse errors) should be distinguished from security-based inconclusive verdicts in the final result calculation
Consider implementing a 'partial success' state where successfully reviewed files contribute to the verdict even if other files fail due to tool errors
